G.evidence: Providence as corrective input (controller output) that drives the system toward the setpoint — grace as the source-field curvature that governs the trajectory.

M.evidence: Human transfer function G_human(s) — personality, capacities, tendencies, choices, will. The plant dynamics that the controller works through.

E.evidence: Energy is implicit in the control system's operation (controller output, disturbance energy). The energetic substrate of the feedback loop.

S.evidence: Strong Force / Love — binding, confinement. The loop gain 'greater is he who is in you' (1 John 4:4) as the binding force that attenuates disturbances.

T.evidence: Thermodynamics / Judgment — entropy, cost, free energy. Sin as deviation (error signal), discipline as stabilization, positive feedback as destabilization (Romans 1:24-28). Entropy production in open-loop systems.

K.evidence: Knowledge / Logos — information, compression, intelligibility. The setpoint R_telos(s) as divine purpose, the error signal as information about deviation. Controllability and observability as knowledge of the system state.

R.evidence: Relativity / Relationship — frame structure, proper time. The relationship between controller and plant, the frame of reference for the feedback loop. The three temporal modes (proportional, integral, derivative) as time-structuring.

Q.evidence: Quantum / Faith — measurement, selection, collapse. The feedback sensor H_conscience(s) as measurement of deviation. The Nyquist stability criterion as a condition for collapse (apostasy). Faith as the selection of the setpoint.

F.evidence: Weak Force / Sin-Conservation — moral decay, conserved deficit. The error signal as sin (conserved deficit that must be corrected). The integral term accumulates past errors — sin's cumulative effect.

C.evidence: Coherence / Christ — global integration operator. C wraps the integral: the entire closed-loop system is the providential governance that integrates all modes. Christ as the setpoint (Romans 8:29 'conformed to the image of his Son') and the controller output.

theological_structure.trinity_structure: Three temporal modes of providence (proportional, integral, derivative) as three aspects of one governance — Father (source/setpoint), Son (mediator/controller output), Spirit (power/presence in the loop).

father_aspect.evidence: Setpoint R_telos(s) as divine purpose (Romans 8:28-29). Source of the reference signal.

son_aspect.evidence: Christ as the setpoint (Romans 8:29) and the controller output (grace). The mediator between the setpoint and the plant.

spirit_aspect.evidence: The loop gain and the power that attenuates disturbances (1 John 4:4). The presence that works through the plant dynamics.

axiom_alignment.strongest_axiom_connection: A1.1 (Existence) — the existence of the feedback loop as the structure of providence
